10.1002_aenm.202570021: Water Splitting In article number 2403744, Rui Liu and co-workers report active CeO2@CoOOH interfaces reconstructed from CeO2@CoSe2 nanoneedles to boost the oxygen evolution reaction (OER) for water splitting. CeO2 facilitates the adsorption of OH− at the CeO2@CoSe2 interfaces and leads to a facile transformation of CoSe2 into CoOOH. The in situ formed CeO2@CoOOH interfaces demonstrate a superior OER performance.
10.1002_aenm.71331: Developing oxygen evolution reaction (OER) catalysts that balance high activity and long‐term durability remains a key challenge for alkaline water electrolysis. Herein, we report a perovskite‐dominant Ag/NiO multiphase composite catalyst derived from nominal Sr 0.8 Ag 0.2 Co 0.6 Fe 0.2 Ni 0.2 O 3‐δ (SACFN2), featuring in situ segregation of Ag and NiO nanophases on a defect‐rich perovskite matrix through self‐driven lattice reconstruction. A‐site Ag + exsolution creates oxygen vacancies and lattice distortion, facilitating B‐site Ni migration and surface NiO segregation. Under OER conditions, NiO nanophases reconstruct toward NiOOH/(Ni,Co,Fe)O(OH)‐like active species, while Ag‐containing domains promote charge redistribution and stabilize the Ag/NiO–perovskite interface. SACFN2 achieves an overpotential of 231 mV at 10 mA cm −2 , a Tafel slope of 51.28 mV dec −1 , and sustained operation over 1000 h at 100 mA cm −2 . Furthermore, anion exchange membrane water electrolyzer (AEMWE) testing with SACFN2 as the anode and Pt/C as the cathode demonstrates stable long‐term operation at 500 mA cm −2 for 1000 h, with only a 54 mV voltage increase. Structural analyses confirm a stable Ag/NiO–perovskite composite interface and oxygen‐deficient lattice framework, demonstrating the value of perovskite‐based multiphase interface and defect engineering for alkaline OER catalysis.
10.1002_smll.74342: Motivated by the high capacity and energy enabled by the two‐electron donation of earth‐abundant magnesium, we developed a novel, generally applicable screening method to evaluate 1,2‐diketone‐based redox units as n‐type cathode active materials (CAMs) for rechargeable magnesium batteries (RMBs). Preliminary DFT calculations (redox potentials, charge density mapping) and cyclic voltammetry in supporting and magnesium electrolyte solutions were used to screen exemplary diketone classes, eliminating unsuitable candidates and identifying phenanthrenequinone (PNQ) as the most promising redox unit for incorporation into a vinylic polymer. Non‐conjugated PNQ‐based vinylic polymers were successfully synthesized, characterized, and tested as CAMs at the coin‐cell level. Non‐optimized Mg‐PNQ cells delivered a starting capacity of up to 77 mAh g −1 , two high‐voltage discharge plateaus at 2.2 and 1.7 V vs . Mg 2 + /Mg, and capacity retentions of 65% after 50 cycles and 50% after 100 cycles, typical for Mg‐quinone systems. A novel electrolyte, [Mg 2 (Ohfip) 3 ][Al(Ohfip) 4 ] in DME, further improved performance to 91 mAh g −1 with 72% retention after 50 cycles. These results demonstrate that the presented screening methodology efficiently identifies suitable CAM candidates within broad substance classes and is readily transferable to further materials.
10.1016_j.memsci.2026.126172: While recovering dissolved methane (D-CH 4 ) from anaerobic effluents supports industrial decarbonization, achieving process sustainability remains a challenge due to the heavy reliance on hazardous solvents for membrane production. This study evaluates a low-toxicity fabrication route for poly(vinylidene fluoride) (PVDF) electrospun membranes using a dimethyl sulfoxide/acetone (DMSO/Ac) solvent system. An optimized water immersion strategy was developed to address systematic residual solvent retention in industrial-scale fibrous layers (thickness > 170 μm) resulting from the low volatility of DMSO. This route reduced the fabrication-to-operation cycle to ∼16 h, an 83% improvement over the method that uses only sweeping air while preserving a defect-free fibrous structure. Consolidation via hot pressing (HP) resulted in a 0.8 to 1.2 μm pore size distribution and increased the PVDF crystallinity (up to 46%). DMSO/Ac-based membranes achieved a dissolved-methane recovery efficiency (RE CH4 ) of ∼50%, performing comparably to commercial and DMF-based alternatives. Performance test (>300 h) using real anaerobic digestate showed a RE CH4 decline to ∼22% after 191 h, primarily due to the deposition of foulants. Chemical cleaning with citric acid and sonication proved effective in removing a significant fraction of reversible fouling and partially restoring the membrane surface properties, demonstrating potential for industrial implementation of these membranes in waste-to-energy applications while improving production safety.
10.1021_acsami.4c22684: P2-type Mn–Fe–Cu-based cathode materials have garnered enormous attention as potential candidates for sodium-ion batteries (SIBs). Nevertheless, the detrimental phase transition and irreversible oxygen release cause significant capacity degradation and poor cycling stability, thereby decelerating their application progress. Herein, we develop a novel P2–Na 0.65 Ca 0.05 Mn 0.55 Co 0.05 Fe 0.2 Cu 0.2 O 2 cathode material via codoping with Co and Ca ions. The incorporation of Co 3+ ions into the Mn sites not only mitigates the Jahn–Teller distortion of Mn 3+ ions to hinder the phase transition but also activates the anionic redox activity by establishing a stable CoO 6 octahedron. The substitution of Ca 2+ ions into the Na sites enhances the stability of the Na + transport pathway and suppresses the sliding of the TMO 2 layers by constructing a stronger Ca–O bond. Under the synergistic effect of the Co/Ca codoping, P2–Na 0.65 Ca 0.05 Mn 0.55 Co 0.05 Fe 0.2 Cu 0.2 O 2 shows enhanced Na + diffusion kinetics, improved intrinsic conductivity, alleviated electrolyte corrosion, and decreased cell volume variation during the Na + extraction/insertion. Consequently, the codoping electrode exhibits a high initial discharge capacity (125.9 mA h g –1 at 0.2 C), an excellent rate performance (79.6 mA h g –1 at 10 C), and an outstanding long-cycle stability (73.2% capacity retention after 1000 cycles at 10 C). This codoping strategy highlights a promising opportunity to advance the practical application of P2-type Mn–Fe–Cu-based cathode materials in high-performance SIBs.
10.1021_acsami.6c08585: The electrochemical reduction of nitrite (NO 2 – ) to ammonia (NH 3 ) offers a promising strategy for simultaneously purifying wastewater and producing value-added chemicals. The metal active site struggles to simultaneously optimize the adsorption strengths of NO 2 – and H*, resulting in a mismatch between the kinetics of intermediate activation and hydrogenation. In this work, we construct a composite catalyst of NiSS-COF/Pd ICs, which enhances the catalytic performance by precisely incorporating nickel single sites (NiSS) and Pd metal-isolated clusters (Pd ICs) into covalent organic frameworks. Thus, NiSS-COF/Pd ICs exhibit an NH 3 production rate of 20.9 mg h –1 mg cat –1 and a high NH 3 Faradaic efficiency of 95.5% at −1.0 V (vs RHE). With −1.3 V applied, NiSS-COF/Pd ICs yielded 35.3 mg h –1 mg cat –1 NH 3, the turnover number reached 58421, and the turnover frequency was 3436.8 h –1 per Ni. The NiSS tunes electronic structures to boost NO 2 – adsorption, while Pd ICs generate H* via these H* migrate to Ni sites, facilitating rapid hydrogenation and synergistic catalysis. As a result, the NiSS-COF/Pd ICs catalyst enables efficient electrochemical conversion of NO 2 – to NH 3, delivering high Faradaic efficiency and enhanced NH 3 production. Overall, this work presents a novel design strategy for developing synergistic catalytic systems that integrate single sites with metal-isolated clusters.
